objects.definition: typedef void *plist_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a node in a property list. Internally refers to any plist node (dict, array, string, int, etc.). Memory is managed via plist_free() and creation helpers like plist_new_*().

objects.definition: typedef void* plist_dict_iter;
objects.description: Opaque iterator handle used to iterate over dictionary (PLIST_DICT) entries. Allocated by plist_dict_new_iter() and freed with standard free().

objects.definition: typedef void* plist_array_iter;
objects.description: Opaque iterator handle used to iterate over array (PLIST_ARRAY) items. Allocated by plist_array_new_iter() and freed with standard free().

objects.definition:
typedef enum
    {
        PLIST_NONE =-1, /**< No type */
        PLIST_BOOLEAN,  /**< Boolean, scalar type */
        PLIST_INT,      /**< Integer, scalar type */
        PLIST_REAL,     /**< Real, scalar type */
        PLIST_STRING,   /**< ASCII string, scalar type */
        PLIST_ARRAY,    /**< Ordered array, structured type */
        PLIST_DICT,     /**< Unordered dictionary (key/value pair), structured type */
        PLIST_DATE,     /**< Date, scalar type */
        PLIST_DATA,     /**< Binary data, scalar type */
        PLIST_KEY,      /**< Key in dictionaries (ASCII String), scalar type */
        PLIST_UID,      /**< Special type used for 'keyed encoding' */
        PLIST_NULL,     /**< NULL type */
    } plist_type;
objects.description: Enumeration of node types that a plist_t can represent. Used with plist_get_node_type() and PLIST_IS_* macros. Note: PLIST_UINT is a backward-compatibility macro aliasing PLIST_INT value, not a separate type.
Enumeration of libplist function return codes. 0 indicates success; negative values indicate specific error conditions.
Enumeration of plist serialization formats accepted/produced by libplist.
Bitfield enumeration for writer options when exporting plists with plist_write_to_* APIs.

PList::Array is a node type representing a property-list array for the C++ binding. It derives from Structure (declared in plist/Structure.h) and manages an ordered collection of child Node pointers using an internal std::vector<Node*>. It provides indexing, front/back accessors, STL-like begin/end iterators (both const and non-const), size query, and methods to append, insert, remove, and clone elements. It also offers templated at/At helpers that cast stored Node* to a requested derived type. Ownership/lifetime semantics of Node* elements are not explicitly documented here; based on typical container wrappers, Array likely manages children as part of the plist tree, but details (e.g., deep copy behavior, destruction responsibility) are unknown from this header alone.

objects.definition: typedef std::vector<Node*>::iterator iterator;
objects.description: Iterator type alias for iterating over the elements of PList::Array. It is the same as std::vector<Node*>::iterator for the internal storage. This is a type alias, not a standalone object; pointer form shown per requirements.

objects.definition: typedef std::vector<Node*>::const_iterator const_iterator;
objects.description: Const iterator type alias for iterating over elements of PList::Array. It maps to std::vector<Node*>::const_iterator of the internal storage. This is a type alias, not a standalone object; pointer form shown per requirements.

C++ class representing a Boolean node in the PList object model. It derives from PList::Node and encapsulates a boolean value within a property list. Constructors allow creating an empty/child-attached boolean node, wrapping an existing plist_t node, copying, assignment, and constructing from a bool. Provides getters/setters for the boolean value and cloning support. Exact ownership and memory semantics of plist_t and Node are defined elsewhere in the library and are not shown here.

C++ class representing a plist data node within the PList namespace. It derives from Node (defined elsewhere) and encapsulates an opaque byte buffer value. Provides constructors from a parent Node pointer, an existing plist_t node, a byte vector, or a raw buffer and size; supports copy/assignment, cloning, setting, and retrieving the data payload. Exact ownership semantics of parent and plist_t are not documented here and must be inferred from the broader library.

Date node type in the PList namespace, deriving from Node. It represents an Apple property list date node. Provides constructors including default (optionally with a parent Node), from an existing plist_t node, copy constructor, and from a 64-bit integer timestamp; offers Clone, SetValue, and GetValue to manipulate the stored date value. Exact epoch and semantics are not documented in this header; based on typical plist conventions, it likely stores seconds relative to the Apple epoch (2001-01-01), but this is not confirmed here.

C++ class representing a dictionary structure in the PList namespace. It derives from Structure (declared elsewhere) and stores key/value pairs where keys are std::string and values are pointers to Node. Provides map-like access (operator[]), iterators (iterator, const_iterator), search (Find), insertion/assignment (Set), removal (Remove), size query, and a key lookup for a given node. Constructors accept an optional parent Node or an existing plist_t node. Lifetime and ownership semantics are not documented here; from the private member _map of Node* values, Dictionary appears to manage a collection of Node pointers keyed by strings.

C++ class representing an integer node in the PList binding, derived from Node. It wraps a plist integer value and offers constructors from signed/unsigned 64-bit integers and from an existing plist_t node, along with getters/setters and a negativity check. Lifetime and storage details are not visible here; destruction is via virtual destructor. Behavior of Clone and ownership semantics follow Node base class, which is declared elsewhere.

C++ wrapper class for a plist key node in the PList namespace. Inherits from Node and represents a key (string name) used in dictionary entries of a property list. Provides constructors from a parent Node, an existing plist_t node, a copy, and a std::string value. Offers methods to clone the node, set the key string, and get the key string. Exact ownership, lifetime rules, and how it interacts with underlying plist_t are inferred; details not specified in this header.

Abstract base class in namespace PList that wraps a libplist (plist.h) node handle (plist_t). It provides virtual cloning, accessors for parent, type, and underlying plist_t, and factory construction from a raw plist_t. Constructors are protected, making Node abstract and intended to be subclassed by concrete plist node types; ownership of the underlying plist_t and parent relationship is managed internally via _node and _parent. Details about memory management semantics (retain/release rules of plist_t) are not specified in this header and must be inferred from libplist usage.

Opaque C handle type from libplist referenced by this header. This header does not define it; it is included from <plist/plist.h>. Ignored for extraction per instructions, but listed here to note missing definition. No further info available in this header.

Enumeration type from libplist referenced by this header to represent the type of a plist node. Not defined in this header; declared in <plist/plist.h>. Ignored for extraction per instructions, but listed here to note missing definition.

C++ class representing a real (double-precision) value node within the PList hierarchy. It derives from PList::Node and provides constructors to wrap an existing plist_t node, copy/assign from another Real, construct from a double, and optionally associate a parent Node. It offers getters/setters for the stored double and a Clone method that returns a new Node copy. Implementation details, ownership semantics, and lifetime rules are not specified in this header; they likely mirror other PList Node derivatives.

C++ wrapper class for a plist string node within the PList namespace. Inherits from Node (declared elsewhere) and represents a string value in a property list. Provides constructors from parent Node, an existing plist_t node, std::string, and C string, as well as copy/assignment, cloning, and getters/setters for the underlying string value. Details of memory management and ownership of the underlying plist_t are governed by the base Node implementation, which is not defined in this header.

Abstract base class for composite PList node types in the C++ binding. It derives from PList::Node and represents structured containers (e.g., dictionary/array-like nodes). Provides serialization to XML and binary forms, size querying, protected constructors for controlled creation, and static factory methods to construct a Structure from XML/binary/memory buffers. The Remove method is pure virtual, requiring derived classes to implement element removal semantics. Ownership and parent-child relationships are managed via UpdateNodeParent. Copying is disabled via private copy constructor/assignment. Details of concrete subclasses and plist_type are not defined in this header.

C++ wrapper class representing a UID node type within the PList namespace. It derives from Node (declared in <plist/Node.h>) and encapsulates a 64-bit unsigned identifier value. Constructors allow creating an empty UID under an optional parent Node, wrapping an existing plist_t node, copying another Uid, or initializing from a uint64_t. Provides cloning and getter/setter for the UID value. Implementation details (memory ownership and backing plist node handling) are not present in this header and must be inferred from the Node base class; exact construction/destruction semantics beyond standard C++ object lifetime are unknown here.

functions.name: plist_new_dict
functions.description: Create a new root plist node of type PLIST_DICT (empty dictionary).
requirements: No arguments.
Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: plist_new_array
functions.description: Create a new root plist node of type PLIST_ARRAY (empty array).
requirements: No arguments.
Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: plist_new_string
functions.description: Create a new PLIST_STRING node with UTF-8 content copied from val.
requirements: val should point to a UTF-8, NULL-terminated string.
Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: plist_new_bool
functions.description: Create a new PLIST_BOOLEAN node with boolean value (0 = false, non-zero = true).
requirements: Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: plist_new_uint
functions.description: Create a new PLIST_INT node initialized with an unsigned integer value (internally stored as uint64_t).
requirements: Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.
Use plist_get_uint_val() or plist_get_int_val() to retrieve value appropriately.

functions.name: plist_new_int
functions.description: Create a new PLIST_INT node initialized with a signed integer value (internally stored as uint64_t).
requirements: Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.
Use plist_get_uint_val() or plist_get_int_val() to retrieve value appropriately.

functions.name: plist_new_real
functions.description: Create a new PLIST_REAL node with given double value.
requirements: Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: plist_new_data
functions.signature: PLIST_API plist_t plist_new_data(const char *val, uint64_t length);
functions.description: Create a new PLIST_DATA node with a copy of the provided binary buffer.
requirements: val must point to at least length bytes of data (length may be 0).
Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: plist_new_unix_date
functions.description: Create a new PLIST_DATE node from a UNIX timestamp (seconds since 1970-01-01).
requirements: Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: plist_new_uid
functions.description: Create a new PLIST_UID node with the given unsigned value.
requirements: Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: plist_new_null
functions.description: Create a new PLIST_NULL node. Note: not valid for all formats (e.g. XML does not support it).
requirements: Returned plist_t must be released with plist_free() when no longer needed.
Be aware some output formats cannot represent PLIST_NULL.

functions.name: plist_free
functions.description: Recursively free a plist node and all of its children.
requirements: plist may be NULL (behavior unspecified in header); when non-NULL, it must be a plist_t obtained from libplist and not freed already.
Do not use to free buffers returned by functions that require plist_mem_free().

functions.name: plist_copy
functions.description: Return a deep copy of the given node and its children.
requirements: node should be a valid plist_t.
Returned plist must be released with plist_free().

functions.name: plist_array_get_size
functions.description: Return the number of items in a PLIST_ARRAY node.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_ARRAY for a meaningful result.

functions.name: plist_array_get_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API plist_t plist_array_get_item(plist_t node, uint32_t n);
functions.description: Get the nth item from a PLIST_ARRAY.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_ARRAY.
n must be in range [0, array_size).
Caller must not free the returned child separately; it is owned by the array.

functions.name: plist_array_get_item_index
functions.description: Get the index of an item that is a member of a PLIST_ARRAY.
requirements: node must be a child of a PLIST_ARRAY.
Returns UINT_MAX if index cannot be determined.

functions.name: plist_array_set_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_array_set_item(plist_t node, plist_t item, uint32_t n);
functions.description: Replace the item at index n in a PLIST_ARRAY with a new item. The previous item is freed.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_ARRAY.
n must be in range [0, array_size); function asserts if out of range.
After insertion the array owns item and will free it when no longer needed.
Do not reuse item pointer after passing it in unless documented otherwise.

functions.name: plist_array_append_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_array_append_item(plist_t node, plist_t item);
functions.description: Append a new item to the end of a PLIST_ARRAY. The array takes ownership of the item.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_ARRAY.
After appending, the array is responsible for freeing item; caller must not free item separately.

functions.name: plist_array_insert_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_array_insert_item(plist_t node, plist_t item, uint32_t n);
functions.description: Insert a new item at position n in a PLIST_ARRAY. The array takes ownership of the item.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_ARRAY.
n must be in range [0, array_size); function asserts if out of range.
After insertion, the array frees item when no longer needed.

functions.name: plist_array_remove_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_array_remove_item(plist_t node, uint32_t n);
functions.description: Remove the item at position n from a PLIST_ARRAY and free it.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_ARRAY.
n must be in range [0, array_size); function asserts if out of range.

functions.name: plist_array_item_remove
functions.description: Remove a node that is a child of a PLIST_ARRAY and free it.
requirements: node must be a child of a PLIST_ARRAY.

functions.name: plist_array_new_iter
functions.description: Create an iterator for a PLIST_ARRAY. Iterator must be freed with free().
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_ARRAY.
iter must be a valid pointer to receive the iterator.
Caller must free the created iterator with the standard free() function.

functions.name: plist_array_next_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_array_next_item(plist_t node, plist_array_iter iter, plist_t *item);
functions.description: Advance an array iterator and retrieve the current item. Sets item to NULL when no more elements remain. Caller must not free returned item.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_ARRAY.
iter must be a valid iterator created by plist_array_new_iter().
item must be a valid pointer to receive results.
Caller must not free the returned item; ownership stays with the array.

functions.name: plist_dict_get_size
functions.description: Return the number of key/value pairs in a PLIST_DICT.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_DICT for a meaningful result.

functions.name: plist_dict_new_iter
functions.description: Create an iterator for a PLIST_DICT. Iterator must be freed with free().
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_DICT.
iter must be a valid pointer to receive the iterator.
Caller must free the created iterator with the standard free() function.

functions.name: plist_dict_next_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_dict_next_item(plist_t node, plist_dict_iter iter, char **key, plist_t *val);
functions.description: Advance a dict iterator, returning key and value for the current pair. Sets val to NULL when exhausted. Caller must free the returned key string; must not free val.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_DICT.
iter must be a valid iterator created by plist_dict_new_iter().
If key is non-NULL, it must point to a char* that will receive an allocated C-string; caller must free it (standard free()).
If val is non-NULL, it must point to a plist_t to receive the value; caller must not free it.

functions.name: plist_dict_get_item_key
functions.description: Retrieve the key string for a dictionary item (child of a PLIST_DICT). Caller must free the returned string.
requirements: node must be an item within a PLIST_DICT.
key must be a valid char** to receive an allocated string.
Caller must free the returned string (use plist_mem_free() as noted for allocated memory).

functions.name: plist_dict_get_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API plist_t plist_dict_get_item(plist_t node, const char* key);
functions.description: Look up and return the value node for a given key in a PLIST_DICT. Caller should not free the returned node.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a NULL-terminated C-string.
Returned node is owned by the dictionary; do not free it.

functions.name: plist_dict_item_get_key
functions.description: Return the PLIST_KEY node associated with a dictionary item. Returns NULL if not applicable.
requirements: node must be a member of a PLIST_DICT for a meaningful result.
Caller must not free the returned key node separately (owned by the dictionary).

functions.name: plist_dict_set_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_dict_set_item(plist_t node, const char* key, plist_t item);
functions.description: Insert or replace a key/value pair in a PLIST_DICT. Previous item for the key is freed. Dictionary takes ownership of item.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a NULL-terminated C-string.
After setting, the dictionary owns item and will free it; caller must not free item.

functions.name: plist_dict_remove_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_dict_remove_item(plist_t node, const char* key);
functions.description: Remove a key/value pair from a PLIST_DICT and free the removed value.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must name an existing entry; function asserts if key is not present.

functions.name: plist_dict_merge
functions.description: Merge all key/value pairs from source dictionary into target dictionary, overwriting existing keys in target.
requirements: target must point to an existing node of type PLIST_DICT.
source must be a node of type PLIST_DICT.

functions.name: plist_dict_get_bool
functions.signature: PLIST_API uint8_t plist_dict_get_bool(plist_t dict, const char *key);
functions.description: Retrieve a boolean value for key from a PLIST_DICT. Accepts PLIST_BOOLEAN, string 'true'/'false', integer 0/>=1, or one-byte data 0/>=1. Returns 0 otherwise.
requirements: dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a NULL-terminated C-string.

functions.name: plist_dict_get_int
functions.signature: PLIST_API int64_t plist_dict_get_int(plist_t dict, const char *key);
functions.description: Retrieve a signed integer value for key from a PLIST_DICT. Accepts PLIST_INT, numeric string (decimal or hex), or DATA of size 1,2,4,8 (little-endian). Returns 0 on mismatch or missing.
requirements: dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a NULL-terminated C-string.

functions.name: plist_dict_get_uint
functions.signature: PLIST_API uint64_t plist_dict_get_uint(plist_t dict, const char *key);
functions.description: Retrieve an unsigned integer value for key from a PLIST_DICT. Accepts PLIST_INT, numeric string (decimal or hex), or DATA of size 1,2,4,8 (little-endian). Returns 0 on mismatch or missing.
requirements: dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a NULL-terminated C-string.

functions.name: plist_dict_copy_item
functions.signature: PLIST_API plist_err_t plist_dict_copy_item(plist_t target_dict, plist_t source_dict, const char *key, const char *alt_source_key);
functions.description: Copy a node from source_dict into target_dict under key. Looks up source by key or alt_source_key (if non-NULL). Fails if neither exists.
requirements: target_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
source_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a NULL-terminated C-string for the destination entry.
alt_source_key may be NULL or a C-string.
Returns PLIST_ERR_SUCCESS on success; PLIST_ERR_INVALID_ARG if source entry absent.

functions.name: plist_dict_copy_bool
functions.signature: PLIST_API plist_err_t plist_dict_copy_bool(plist_t target_dict, plist_t source_dict, const char *key, const char *alt_source_key);
functions.description: Copy a boolean value from source_dict into target_dict under key. Value is read using plist_dict_get_bool and created as PLIST_BOOLEAN.
requirements: target_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
source_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a destination key string; alt_source_key may be NULL.
Returns PLIST_ERR_SUCCESS on success; PLIST_ERR_INVALID_ARG if source entry absent.

functions.name: plist_dict_copy_int
functions.signature: PLIST_API plist_err_t plist_dict_copy_int(plist_t target_dict, plist_t source_dict, const char *key, const char *alt_source_key);
functions.description: Copy a signed integer value from source_dict into target_dict under key. Value read with plist_dict_get_int and created as PLIST_INT.
requirements: target_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
source_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a destination key string; alt_source_key may be NULL.
Returns PLIST_ERR_SUCCESS on success; PLIST_ERR_INVALID_ARG if source entry absent.

functions.name: plist_dict_copy_uint
functions.signature: PLIST_API plist_err_t plist_dict_copy_uint(plist_t target_dict, plist_t source_dict, const char *key, const char *alt_source_key);
functions.description: Copy an unsigned integer value from source_dict into target_dict under key. Value read with plist_dict_get_uint and created as PLIST_INT.
requirements: target_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
source_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a destination key string; alt_source_key may be NULL.
Returns PLIST_ERR_SUCCESS on success; PLIST_ERR_INVALID_ARG if source entry absent.

functions.name: plist_dict_copy_data
functions.signature: PLIST_API plist_err_t plist_dict_copy_data(plist_t target_dict, plist_t source_dict, const char *key, const char *alt_source_key);
functions.description: Copy a PLIST_DATA node from source_dict into target_dict under key. Fails if the source node is not PLIST_DATA.
requirements: target_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
source_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a destination key string; alt_source_key may be NULL.
Returns PLIST_ERR_SUCCESS on success; PLIST_ERR_INVALID_ARG if source missing or not PLIST_DATA.

functions.name: plist_dict_copy_string
functions.signature: PLIST_API plist_err_t plist_dict_copy_string(plist_t target_dict, plist_t source_dict, const char *key, const char *alt_source_key);
functions.description: Copy a PLIST_STRING node from source_dict into target_dict under key. Fails if the source node is not PLIST_STRING.
requirements: target_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
source_dict must be of type PLIST_DICT.
key must be a destination key string; alt_source_key may be NULL.
Returns PLIST_ERR_SUCCESS on success; PLIST_ERR_INVALID_ARG if source missing or not PLIST_STRING.

functions.name: plist_get_parent
functions.description: Return the parent node of a node (NULL for root).
requirements: node should be a valid plist_t.

functions.name: plist_get_node_type
functions.description: Return the plist_type of a node.
requirements: node should be a valid plist_t.

functions.name: plist_get_key_val
functions.description: Retrieve the C-string value of a PLIST_KEY node, allocating memory for it. No-op if node is not PLIST_KEY.
requirements: node should be a PLIST_KEY for a meaningful result.
val must be a valid char** to receive an allocated string.
Caller must free the allocated string using plist_mem_free().

functions.name: plist_get_string_val
functions.description: Retrieve the UTF-8 C-string value of a PLIST_STRING node, allocating memory for it. No-op if node is not PLIST_STRING.
requirements: node should be a PLIST_STRING for a meaningful result.
val must be a valid char** to receive an allocated string.
Caller must free the allocated string using plist_mem_free().

functions.name: plist_get_string_ptr
functions.signature: PLIST_API const char* plist_get_string_ptr(plist_t node, uint64_t* length);
functions.description: Get a direct pointer to the internal buffer of a PLIST_STRING node (NULL-terminated). Do not modify; valid only while the node exists.
requirements: node must be of type PLIST_STRING for a meaningful result.
If length is non-NULL, it will be set to the string length.
Caller must not free or modify the returned pointer; copy if needed.

functions.name: plist_get_bool_val
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_get_bool_val(plist_t node, uint8_t * val);
functions.description: Retrieve the value of a PLIST_BOOLEAN node into val. No-op if node is not PLIST_BOOLEAN.
requirements: node should be PLIST_BOOLEAN for meaningful result.
val must be a valid uint8_t*.

functions.name: plist_get_uint_val
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_get_uint_val(plist_t node, uint64_t * val);
functions.description: Retrieve the unsigned integer value of a PLIST_INT node into val. No-op if node is not PLIST_INT.
requirements: node should be PLIST_INT for meaningful result.
val must be a valid uint64_t*.

functions.name: plist_get_int_val
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_get_int_val(plist_t node, int64_t * val);
functions.description: Retrieve the signed integer value of a PLIST_INT node into val. No-op if node is not PLIST_INT.
requirements: node should be PLIST_INT for meaningful result.
val must be a valid int64_t*.

functions.name: plist_get_real_val
functions.description: Retrieve the double value of a PLIST_REAL node into val. No-op if node is not PLIST_REAL.
requirements: node should be PLIST_REAL for meaningful result.
val must be a valid double*.

functions.name: plist_get_data_val
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_get_data_val(plist_t node, char **val, uint64_t * length);
functions.description: Retrieve a copy of the data buffer of a PLIST_DATA node (allocates new buffer). No-op if node is not PLIST_DATA.
requirements: node should be PLIST_DATA for meaningful result.
val must be a valid char** to receive an allocated buffer; caller must free with plist_mem_free().
length must be a valid uint64_t* to receive size.

functions.name: plist_get_data_ptr
functions.signature: PLIST_API const char* plist_get_data_ptr(plist_t node, uint64_t* length);
functions.description: Get a direct pointer to the internal data buffer of a PLIST_DATA node. Do not modify; valid only while the node exists.
requirements: node must be PLIST_DATA for meaningful result.
length must be a valid uint64_t* to receive the length.
Caller must not free or modify returned pointer; copy if needed.

functions.name: plist_get_unix_date_val
functions.description: Retrieve the UNIX timestamp (seconds since 1970) from a PLIST_DATE node. No-op if node is not PLIST_DATE.
requirements: node should be PLIST_DATE for meaningful result.
sec must be a valid int64_t*.

functions.name: plist_get_uid_val
functions.signature: PLIST_API void plist_get_uid_val(plist_t node, uint64_t * val);
functions.description: Retrieve the value of a PLIST_UID node. No-op if node is not PLIST_UID.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces UTF-8, length-prefixed strings suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# It avoids embedding literal NUL bytes in the source and in the produced payload strings.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

TOKENS = [
    "k", "key", "value", "true", "false", "TRUE", "FALSE", "0", "1",
    "a", "b", "c", "dst", "src", "ssrc", "sdst",
    # Minimal plist XML
    "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n"
    "<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC \"-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN\" \"http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd\">\n"
    "<plist version=\"1.0\">\n<dict>\n<key>a</key><string>v</string>\n</dict>\n</plist>\n",
    # JSON snippets
    "{\"a\":\"v\"}", "{\n  \"k\": 123, \n  \"b\": true\n}",
    # OpenStep-like
    "{ a = v; }", "(1,2,3)",
    # Substring/contains edge cases
    "x", "xxx", "xy", "yx", "\u2603", "\u00A9",
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "こんにちは",  # Japanese
    "Привет",     # Russian
    "مرحبا",       # Arabic
    "हैलो",        # Hindi
    "γειά",        # Greek
    "🙂🙃😉😊😍",   # Emojis
]


def rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    parts: List[str] = []
    total = 0
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_:/.,+*#@()[]{}<>="
    while total < length:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.7:
            seg_len = max(1, int(rng.expovariate(1.5)))
            seg_len = min(seg_len, length - total)
            seg = "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(seg_len))
            parts.append(seg)
            total += len(seg)
        else:
            s = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
            # Truncate Unicode sample if it would exceed the target length
            if total + len(s) > length:
                s = s[: max(0, length - total)]
            parts.append(s)
            total += len(s)
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Remove defensive NULs if any
    s = s.replace("\x00", "")
    return s


def build_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # Common small keys/values
    out.extend(["k", "key", "dst", "src", "ssrc", "sdst", "a", "b", "c"])

    # Various sizes to hit clamp paths
    out.extend([
        "v",
        "x" * 5,
        "y" * 33,
        "z" * 129,
        "q" * 257,
        "w" * 513,
    ])

    # Hex-like data payload (no NULs)
    data_like = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(64)).hex()
    out.append(data_like)

    # Tokens for comparisons/contains
    out.extend(["match", "nomatch", "prefix", "prefix-suffix", "substr", "needle", "haystack"])

    # XML/JSON/OpenStep fragments
    out.extend([
        "<key>a</key>",
        "<string>v</string>",
        "<dict></dict>",
        "{\"num\":42}",
        "{foo=bar;}",
    ])

    # Random UTF-8 strings of varying lengths
    for _ in range(12):
        out.append(rand_utf8(rng, 1, 64))
    for _ in range(6):
        out.append(rand_utf8(rng, 65, 140))
    for _ in range(3):
        out.append(rand_utf8(rng, 141, 600))

    # Ensure at least one well-formed minimal XML plist
    out.append(
        "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n"
        "<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC \"-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN\" \"http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd\">\n"
        "<plist version=\"1.0\">\n<dict>\n<key>a</key><string>v</string>\n</dict>\n</plist>\n"
    )

    # Shuffle for variety
    rng.shuffle(out)

    # Clean and ensure non-empty strings
    cleaned: List[str] = []
    for s in out:
        s2 = s.replace("\x00", "")
        if not s2:
            s2 = "k"
        cleaned.append(s2)

    return cleaned


def pack_strings(strings: List[str], budget: int) -> bytes:
    # Pack as [uint16_le length][payload]*
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    size = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
        if b.find(b"\x00") != -1:
            b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"")
        if len(b) > 1024:
            b = b[:1024]
        if len(b) > 65535:
            b = b[:65535]
        header = len(b).to_bytes(2, "little")
        need = 2 + len(b)
        if size + need > budget:
            break
        chunks.append(header)
        chunks.append(b)
        size += need
    return b"".join(chunks)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strings = build_strings(rng)
    buf = pack_strings(strings, MAX_TOTAL)
    if not buf:
        fallback = b"k"
        buf = len(fallback).to_bytes(2, "little") + fallback
    return buf

import random
import struct
import zlib
import json
import plistlib
from typing import List

# Generator for an "arbitrary binary blob" tailored to exercise libplist data uses.
# Strategy: produce valid and interesting buffers that can be consumed as:
# - PLIST_DATA payloads (any bytes, including NULs; sizes up to 1024 in stubs)
# - Inputs for heuristic binary-plist detection (plist_is_binary)
# - Inputs to Structure::FromBin / FromMemory (try valid bplist, valid XML, valid JSON, OpenStep-like, or random)
# We assemble a small corpus of constructors and pick based on seed.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Minimal valid binary plist (bplist00) with a small dictionary or array.
# We'll craft a few small, known-good samples produced by Python's plistlib, then embed here
# so that we do not rely on runtime I/O.

def _build_bplist(obj) -> bytes:
    try:
        return plistlib.dumps(obj, fmt=plistlib.FMT_BINARY)
    except Exception:
        # Fallback to a tiny prebuilt header-like sequence won't be valid; so return empty
        return b""

# Minimal valid XML plist

def _build_xml_plist(obj) -> bytes:
    try:
        return plistlib.dumps(obj, fmt=plistlib.FMT_XML)
    except Exception:
        return b""

# OpenStep-like (old-style) plist text. This is not strictly validated by plistlib,
# but libplist has an OpenStep parser. We'll emit a simple dictionary form.

def _build_openstep_plist(entries: List[tuple]) -> bytes:
    # Example: { key = value; key2 = "string with spaces"; num = 42; data = <DEADBEEF>; }
    parts = ["{"]
    for k, v in entries:
        if isinstance(v, bool):
            sv = "YES" if v else "NO"
        elif isinstance(v, (int, float)):
            sv = str(v)
        elif isinstance(v, (bytes, bytearray)):
            sv = "<" + v.hex().upper() + ">"
        else:
            s = str(v)
            if any(c.isspace() for c in s) or any(c in s for c in ['"', "'", "=", ";", "<", ">", "{", "}"]):
                sv = '"' + s.replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
            else:
                sv = s
        parts.append(f" {k} = {sv};")
    parts.append(" }")
    return "".join(parts).encode("utf-8")

# Random binary blob builder with controllable size and entropy.

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

# Build a buffer that contains many byte value patterns to stress compare/contains:

def _patterned_blob(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    chunks = []
    # ASCII segment
    s_len = rng.randrange(0, min(256, max_len//4 + 1))
    if s_len:
        s = ''.join(chr(rng.randrange(32, 127)) for _ in range(s_len)).encode('utf-8')
        chunks.append(s)
    # Zero bytes segment
    z_len = rng.randrange(0, min(256, max_len//4 + 1))
    if z_len:
        chunks.append(b"\x00" * z_len)
    # Incrementing sequence
    inc_len = rng.randrange(0, min(256, max_len//4 + 1))
    if inc_len:
        chunks.append(bytes((i % 256 for i in range(inc_len))))
    # High-entropy chunk
    rem = max(0, max_len - sum(len(c) for c in chunks))
    if rem:
        chunks.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(0, rem + 1)))
    # Optional duplicate to help contains() succeed sometimes
    if chunks:
        dup = rng.choice(chunks)
        chunks.append(dup)
    blob = b"".join(chunks)
    return blob[:max_len]

# Build JSON that libplist can parse: a dict with a data blob encoded as base64 via plistlib-compatible mapping.
# libplist supports JSON straight mapping: strings, numbers, arrays, dicts, booleans, null.
# Data nodes in libplist JSON are often represented as {"$data": "BASE64"} or raw base64 depending on parser.
# For broad compatibility, include strings, numbers, arrays, dicts.

def _build_json(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    obj = {
        "k": "v",
        "n": rng.randrange(0, 1 << 16),
        "b": bool(rng.randrange(0, 2)),
        "arr": [rng.randrange(-1000, 1000), "s", bool(rng.randrange(0, 2))],
        "nested": {"a": 1, "s": "t"}
    }
    data = json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
    if len(data) > max_len:
        return data[:max_len]
    return data

# Precompute a few valid bplists to pick from
_VALID_BPLISTS = [
    _build_bplist({"a": 1, "b": True, "s": "x"}),
    _build_bplist([1, 2, 3, "s", False]),
    _build_bplist({"d": {"k": "v"}, "arr": [0, 1]}),
]
_VALID_XMLS = [
    _build_xml_plist({"a": 1, "b": True, "s": "x"}),
    _build_xml_plist([1, 2, 3, "s", False]),
]

# Construct a minimal bplist header-like prefix combined with content to also tick heuristics
BPLIST_MAGIC = b"bplist00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a mode to target different fuzz stubs paths.
    mode = rng.randrange(0, 8)

    # Size cap for most stubs is 1024; keep under 1024 commonly, but occasionally go larger (still <= 4096).
    typical_cap = 1024

    if mode == 0:
        # Valid binary plist (array or dict)
        candidates = [b for b in _VALID_BPLISTS if b]
        if not candidates:
            # Fallback to random with magic header so plist_is_binary may detect
            body = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(16, typical_cap))
            return (BPLIST_MAGIC + body)[:MAX_SIZE]
        buf = rng.choice(candidates)
        # Optionally append benign trailing bytes to test length handling in is_binary()
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            pad = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randrange(0, 16))
            buf = (buf + pad)[:MAX_SIZE]
        return buf

    if mode == 1:
        # Valid XML plist
        candidates = [b for b in _VALID_XMLS if b]
        if not candidates:
            # Build simple XML manually
            xml = b"<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n" \
                  b"<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC \"-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN\" \"http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd\">\n" \
                  b"<plist version=\"1.0\"><dict><key>k</key><string>v</string></dict></plist>"
            return xml[:MAX_SIZE]
        return candidates[rng.randrange(0, len(candidates))][:MAX_SIZE]

    if mode == 2:
        # OpenStep-like plist text
        entries = [
            ("k", "v"),
            ("n", rng.randrange(0, 1000)),
            ("b", bool(rng.randrange(0, 2))),
        ]
        # Include a short data hex to exercise parser path
        data_len = rng.randrange(0, 16)
        data = _rand_bytes(rng, data_len)
        entries.append(("data", data))
        buf = _build_openstep_plist(entries)
        return buf[:MAX_SIZE]

    if mode == 3:
        # Valid JSON plist-compatible object
        return _build_json(rng, typical_cap)

    if mode == 4:
        # Patterned arbitrary blob for PLIST_DATA payload and comparisons
        max_len = rng.randrange(0, typical_cap + 1)
        return _patterned_blob(rng, max_len)

    if mode == 5:
        # Random bytes with bplist magic to trigger plist_is_binary(heuristic) sometimes
        body_len = rng.randrange(0, typical_cap)
        body = _rand_bytes(rng, body_len)
        # Insert magic at start or offset
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            buf = BPLIST_MAGIC + body
        else:
            off = rng.randrange(0, 8)
            buf = _rand_bytes(rng, off) + BPLIST_MAGIC + body
        return buf[:MAX_SIZE]

    if mode == 6:
        # Small buffer, including empty, to exercise zero-length PLIST_DATA and edge cases
        n = rng.randrange(0, 33)
        # Mix of zeros and small ASCII
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            return b"\x00" * n
        else:
            return bytes((i % 256 for i in range(n)))

    # mode == 7:
    # High-entropy random with occasional compressible segment; good for data_val_contains variety
    total = rng.randrange(1, min(MAX_SIZE, typical_cap) + 1)
    # Build as: [repeated pattern]*k + random tail
    pat_len = max(1, rng.randrange(1, 17))
    pattern = _rand_bytes(rng, pat_len)
    reps = rng.randrange(1, max(2, total // pat_len))
    buf = (pattern * reps)[:total]
    # Random tail
    tail_len = max(0, total - len(buf))
    if tail_len:
        buf += _rand_bytes(rng, tail_len)
    # Occasionally wrap with a small header for variety
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and len(buf) + len(BPLIST_MAGIC) <= MAX_SIZE:
        buf = BPLIST_MAGIC + buf
    return buf[:MAX_SIZE]

import os
import random
import struct
import time
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid property list (plist) byte buffers in a variety of
# formats that libplist can parse via plist_read_from_file / plist_from_memory:
# - Binary plist (bplist00)
# - XML plist
# - JSON plist
# - OpenStep (old-style) plist
# It selects a format seeded-randomly and emits small but diverse documents that
# exercise different node types: array, dict, string, bool, int (signed/unsigned),
# real, data (base64 in XML/JSON/OpenStep), date (UNIX timestamp), uid, and null
# (where format allows). All outputs are <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Utility: base64 (standard library)
import base64


def _rand_bool(rnd: random.Random) -> bool:
    return bool(rnd.getrandbits(1))


def _rand_ints(rnd: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # Produce a pair of interesting signed/unsigned magnitudes
    signed_choices = [
        0,
        1,
        -1,
        2**7 - 1,
        -(2**7),
        2**15 - 1,
        -(2**15),
        2**31 - 1,
        -(2**31),
        2**63 - 1,
        -(2**63) + 1,  # avoid overflow when parsed to int64
    ]
    unsigned_choices = [0, 1, 255, 256, 2**32 - 1, 2**40, 2**63, 2**64 - 1]
    return rnd.choice(signed_choices), rnd.choice(unsigned_choices)


def _rand_real(rnd: random.Random) -> float:
    choices = [0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 1e-9, -1e-9, 1e9, -1e9, 3.1415926535, 2.7182818284]
    # Also a random finite double around normal ranges
    choices.append(rnd.uniform(-1e6, 1e6))
    return rnd.choice(choices)


def _rand_string(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include ASCII and some UTF-8
    fragments = [
        "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "δ", "こんにちは", "emoji_🙂", "key", "value",
        "true", "false", "0x10", "12345", "nested", "array", "dict",
    ]
    s = rnd.choice(fragments)
    # Occasionally append a numeric suffix
    if _rand_bool(rnd):
        s += str(rnd.randint(0, 9999))
    return s


def _rand_bytes(rnd: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=48) -> bytes:
    n = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return rnd.randbytes(n) if hasattr(rnd, 'randbytes') else bytes([rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(n)])


def _rand_unix_time(rnd: random.Random) -> int:
    # Range around typical epoch up to year ~2100 and down to 1970
    now = int(time.time())
    span = 60 * 60 * 24 * 365 * 50  # 50 years
    return rnd.randint(max(0, now - span), now + span)


# JSON generator (accepted by plist_from_json / plist_from_memory)

def _gen_json(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    s_int, u_int = _rand_ints(rnd)
    val_str = _rand_string(rnd)
    val_data = _rand_bytes(rnd, 4, 40)
    ts = _rand_unix_time(rnd)
    realv = _rand_real(rnd)
    b = _rand_bool(rnd)
    uidv = u_int & ((1 << 64) - 1)

    # Represent data as base64 string, date as seconds, uid as special object form
    # libplist JSON expects a simple JSON that maps well into plist types.
    payload = {
        "bool": b,
        "int": s_int,
        "uint": int(u_int),
        "real": realv,
        "string": val_str,
        "data": base64.b64encode(val_data).decode("ascii"),
        "date": ts,
        "uid": {"CF$UID": int(uidv)},
        "array": [b, s_int, realv, val_str, {"CF$UID": int(uidv)}],
        "dict": {"k1": val_str, "k2": int(u_int)},
        # null exists as JSON null; some plist formats may not serialize it back, but parser can accept/convert
        "null": None,
    }

    # Compact vs pretty to vary whitespace
    import json
    if _rand_bool(rnd):
        data = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"))
    else:
        data = json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    out = data.encode("utf-8")
    return out[:MAX_SIZE]


# XML plist generator (Apple plist XML v1.0)

def _xml_escape(s: str) -> str:
    return (
        s.replace("&", "&")
        .replace("<", "<")
        .replace(">", ">")
        .replace('"', """)
        .replace("'", "'")
    )


def _gen_xml(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    s_int, u_int = _rand_ints(rnd)
    val_str = _rand_string(rnd)
    val_data = _rand_bytes(rnd, 3, 32)
    ts = _rand_unix_time(rnd)
    realv = _rand_real(rnd)
    b = _rand_bool(rnd)
    uidv = u_int

    data_b64 = base64.b64encode(val_data).decode("ascii")

    # XML supports true/false, integer, real, string, data, date (ISO8601), uid as <uid>, array, dict
    # Date in libplist XML is seconds since 2001-01-01 or ISO 8601? libplist accepts <date> in ISO 8601.
    # We'll emit ISO 8601 Zulu.
    iso = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(ts))

    parts: List[str] = []
    parts.append("""<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">\n<plist version="1.0">""")
    parts.append("<dict>")
    def kv(key: str, value_xml: str):
        parts.append(f"<key>{_xml_escape(key)}</key>")
        parts.append(value_xml)

    kv("bool", "<true/>" if b else "<false/>")
    kv("int", f"<integer>{s_int}</integer>")
    kv("uint", f"<integer>{u_int}</integer>")
    kv("real", f"<real>{repr(float(realv))}</real>")
    kv("string", f"<string>{_xml_escape(val_str)}</string>")
    kv("data", f"<data>{data_b64}</data>")
    kv("date", f"<date>{iso}</date>")
    kv("uid", f"<uid>{uidv}</uid>")
    parts.append("<key>array</key>")
    parts.append("<array>")
    parts.append("<true/>" if b else "<false/>")
    parts.append(f"<integer>{s_int}</integer>")
    parts.append(f"<real>{repr(float(realv))}</real>")
    parts.append(f"<string>{_xml_escape(val_str)}</string>")
    parts.append(f"<uid>{uidv}</uid>")
    parts.append("</array>")
    parts.append("<key>dict</key>")
    parts.append("<dict>")
    parts.append("<key>k1</key>")
    parts.append(f"<string>{_xml_escape(val_str)}</string>")
    parts.append("<key>k2</key>")
    parts.append(f"<integer>{u_int}</integer>")
    parts.append("</dict>")
    # Note: XML format has no null; omit to keep strictly valid
    parts.append("</dict>")
    parts.append("</plist>")
    xml = "\n".join(parts)
    out = xml.encode("utf-8")
    return out[:MAX_SIZE]


# OpenStep (old-style) generator

def _escape_openstep_string(s: str) -> str:
    # Minimal escaping for quotes and backslashes
    return s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')


def _gen_openstep(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    s_int, u_int = _rand_ints(rnd)
    val_str = _rand_string(rnd)
    val_data = _rand_bytes(rnd, 2, 32)
    realv = _rand_real(rnd)
    b = _rand_bool(rnd)

    # Represent data as <...> hex sequence for OpenStep
    data_hex = val_data.hex()

    # OpenStep format example:
    # {
    #   bool = YES; int = -1; uint = 42; real = 3.14; string = "text"; data = <DEADBEEF>;
    #   array = (YES, -1, 3.14, "text"); dict = {k1 = "v"; k2 = 99;};
    # }
    yesno = "YES" if b else "NO"
    esc = _escape_openstep_string(val_str)
    parts = []
    parts.append("{")
    parts.append(f" bool = {yesno};")
    parts.append(f" int = {s_int};")
    parts.append(f" uint = {u_int};")
    parts.append(f" real = {repr(float(realv))};")
    parts.append(f" string = \"{esc}\";")
    parts.append(f" data = <{data_hex}>;")
    parts.append(" array = (")
    parts.append(f"{yesno}, {s_int}, {repr(float(realv))}, \"{esc}\"");
    parts.append(");")
    parts.append(" dict = {")
    parts.append(f"k1 = \"{esc}\"; k2 = {u_int};")
    parts.append("};")
    parts.append("}")
    txt = "".join(parts)
    return txt.encode("utf-8")[:MAX_SIZE]


# Binary plist generator (bplist00). We'll construct a valid, small binary plist by
# creating an XML/JSON first and then embedding would require external libs, which
# we cannot use. Instead, we handcraft a minimal bplist for a small dict.
# For robustness, we generate a tiny dict with a couple of primitive values.
# Implementation based on Apple bplist specification.

# Helper to build minimal bplist with a dict of keys->values (string, bool, int, real, data)
class BPlistBuilder:
    def __init__(self):
        self.objects: List[bytes] = []

    def _pack_int_obj(self, n: int) -> bytes:
        # integer object: 0x1n where n is power-of-two byte length (0..3 => 1,2,4,8 bytes)
        # choose minimal size from 1,2,4,8
        if -128 <= n <= 255:
            size = 1
        elif -32768 <= n <= 65535:
            size = 2
        elif -2147483648 <= n <= 4294967295:
            size = 4
        else:
            size = 8
        code = {1: 0x10, 2: 0x11, 4: 0x12, 8: 0x13}[size]
        return bytes([code]) + n.to_bytes(size, "big", signed=True)

    def _pack_uint_obj(self, n: int) -> bytes:
        if n <= 0xFF:
            size = 1
        elif n <= 0xFFFF:
            size = 2
        elif n <= 0xFFFFFFFF:
            size = 4
        else:
            size = 8
        code = {1: 0x10, 2: 0x11, 4: 0x12, 8: 0x13}[size]
        return bytes([code]) + n.to_bytes(size, "big", signed=False)

    def _pack_bool(self, b: bool) -> bytes:
        return bytes([0x09 if b else 0x08])

    def _pack_real(self, d: float) -> bytes:
        # 64-bit float
        return bytes([0x23]) + struct.pack(">d", float(d))

    def _pack_data(self, blob: bytes) -> bytes:
        hdr = self._pack_counted_header(0x40, len(blob))
        return hdr + blob

    def _pack_ascii(self, s: str) -> bytes:
        data = s.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")
        hdr = self._pack_counted_header(0x50, len(data))
        return hdr + data

    def _pack_uid(self, n: int) -> bytes:
        # UID object: 0x80 + (size-1), 1..8 bytes
        if n <= 0xFF:
            size = 1
        elif n <= 0xFFFF:
            size = 2
        elif n <= 0xFFFFFFFF:
            size = 4
        else:
            size = 8
        return bytes([0x80 + (size - 1)]) + n.to_bytes(size, "big")

    def _pack_counted_header(self, base: int, count: int) -> bytes:
        # If count < 15, header single byte base|count, else base|0x0F + integer object count
        if count < 15:
            return bytes([base | count])
        else:
            return bytes([base | 0x0F]) + self._pack_uint_obj(count)

    def _pack_array(self, objrefs: List[int], refsize: int) -> bytes:
        hdr = self._pack_counted_header(0xA0, len(objrefs))
        body = b"".join([i.to_bytes(refsize, "big") for i in objrefs])
        return hdr + body

    def _pack_dict(self, keyrefs: List[int], valrefs: List[int], refsize: int) -> bytes:
        hdr = self._pack_counted_header(0xD0, len(keyrefs))
        ks = b"".join([i.to_bytes(refsize, "big") for i in keyrefs])
        vs = b"".join([i.to_bytes(refsize, "big") for i in valrefs])
        return hdr + ks + vs

    def build_simple(self, rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
        # Objects we will include:
        # keys: "bool","int","uint","real","string","data","uid","array","dict"
        # values: respective small primitives
        s_int, u_int = _rand_ints(rnd)
        realv = _rand_real(rnd)
        b = _rand_bool(rnd)
        s = _rand_string(rnd)
        dat = _rand_bytes(rnd, 2, 24)
        uidv = u_int & ((1 << 64) - 1)

        objs: List[bytes] = []
        def add(obj: bytes) -> int:
            objs.append(obj)
            return len(objs) - 1

        # keys as ASCII strings
        k_bool = add(self._pack_ascii("bool"))
        k_int = add(self._pack_ascii("int"))
        k_uint = add(self._pack_ascii("uint"))
        k_real = add(self._pack_ascii("real"))
        k_string = add(self._pack_ascii("string"))
        k_data = add(self._pack_ascii("data"))
        k_uid = add(self._pack_ascii("uid"))
        k_array = add(self._pack_ascii("array"))
        k_dict = add(self._pack_ascii("dict"))

        v_bool = add(self._pack_bool(b))
        # For variety, store signed int possibly negative; and unsigned via positive integer
        v_int = add(self._pack_int_obj(int(s_int)))
        v_uint = add(self._pack_uint_obj(int(u_int)))
        v_real = add(self._pack_real(realv))
        v_string = add(self._pack_ascii(s))
        v_data = add(self._pack_data(dat))
        v_uid = add(self._pack_uid(int(uidv)))
        # small array [bool, int]
        # array will reference existing objects by index; build after they exist
        # placeholder indices will be set later
        # small dict {k1: string}
        k1 = add(self._pack_ascii("k1"))
        v_k1 = add(self._pack_ascii(s))

        # Compute ref size (bytes) based on number of objects to reference
        # We will add array and dict and the toplevel dict later
        # Estimate max objects ~ current + 3
        total_est = len(objs) + 3
        refsize = 1 if total_est <= 0xFF else (2 if total_est <= 0xFFFF else 4)

        v_array = add(self._pack_array([v_bool, v_int], refsize))
        v_idict = add(self._pack_dict([k1], [v_k1], refsize))

        # Top-level dict mapping keys to values
        keyrefs = [k_bool, k_int, k_uint, k_real, k_string, k_data, k_uid, k_array, k_dict]
        valrefs = [v_bool, v_int, v_uint, v_real, v_string, v_data, v_uid, v_array, v_idict]
        top = add(self._pack_dict(keyrefs, valrefs, refsize))

        # Calculate object ref size precisely now
        nobj = len(objs)
        refsize = 1 if nobj <= 0xFF else (2 if nobj <= 0xFFFF else 4)

        # Offsets table
        offset_table: List[int] = []
        body = b""
        for obj in objs:
            offset_table.append(len(body))
            body += obj

        # Header and trailer
        header = b"bplist00"
        offset_table_bytes = b"".join([o.to_bytes(refsize, "big") for o in offset_table])
        offset_table_offset = len(header) + len(body)

        # Trailer: 32 bytes
        # byte 6: offset int size; byte 7: object ref size
        # bytes 8-15: number of objects
        # bytes 16-23: top object index
        # bytes 24-31: offset table offset
        trailer = bytearray(32)
        # offset int size: choose 2 or 4 based on max offset
        max_off = max(offset_table) if offset_table else 0
        offsize = 1
        if max_off > 0xFF:
            offsize = 2 if max_off <= 0xFFFF else 4
        trailer[6] = offsize
        trailer[7] = refsize
        struct.pack_into(">Q", trailer, 8, nobj)
        struct.pack_into(">Q", trailer, 16, top)
        struct.pack_into(">Q", trailer, 24, offset_table_offset)

        # If offsize is not 1, we need to re-encode offset table accordingly
        def enc_off(o: int) -> bytes:
            return o.to_bytes(offsize, "big")
        offset_table_bytes = b"".join(enc_off(o) for o in offset_table)

        out = header + body + offset_table_bytes + bytes(trailer)
        return out


def _gen_binary_plist(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return BPlistBuilder().build_simple(rnd)[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a format to target the fuzzer stubs that read/write files.
    # Weight toward formats the writer may emit (XML, JSON, OpenStep) and also include binary.
    choices = [
        ("xml", _gen_xml),
        ("json", _gen_json),
        ("openstep", _gen_openstep),
        ("bplist", _gen_binary_plist),
    ]
    # Shuffle formats deterministically then pick one
    rnd.shuffle(choices)
    fmt, fn = rnd.choice(choices)
    data = fn(rnd)

    # Ensure not exceeding size and non-empty
    if not data:
        data = b"{}"
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]
